findings.title: Directed Distribution and Affiliation
findings.claim: The focus directs resources to named claimants and forbids waste; the sequel calls wasteful spenders brothers of the distant and ungrateful, so transfer and dispersal contrast as acts that sustain or rupture social claims.
findings.mechanism: The giving imperative meets the holder-owned due and recipient list, while the doubled waste form meets the seed-scattering image. In 17:27 the waste act becomes an actor identity under brotherhood, remoteness, and covering a favor; the tether image supplies an attributed account of how spending can bind or sever relations.
findings.reader_payoff: A flat list of spending rules becomes a relation among who receives, where resources go, and the affiliation wasteful conduct expresses.
findings.containment: The literal duty to give and prohibition on squandering remain intact. Seed scatter is an analogy; tether, remoteness, and covering images are contextual or attributed layers, and the verses do not claim that every expense expresses the spender's identity.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence directly supplies the due-versus-waste and seed image; an exact but legacy_unbound HFT trace adds the affiliation reading. The context coordinates match the packet, while the source-image branches remain explicitly attributed.

findings.title: Ethical Proximity and Paths
findings.claim: The focus's kin and wayfarer name claim-bearing closeness and movement; 17:32 uses the same proximity and path vocabulary around a forbidden act and calls its path bad, making destination and relation matter to how movement is read.

The later approach prohibition and evaluated path return through those focus words, creating a contrast between proximity that generates a due and approach that must be stopped, and between a traveler and a condemned path.
findings.reader_payoff: Nearness and travel become morally differentiated by what relation or destination they serve, while the recipients keep their literal identities.
findings.containment: This is a contextual topology, not a shared lexical definition across the verses. The traveler is not equated with the prohibited act, and the focus's ordinary recipient reading stays intact.

epistemic.reason: The roots and coordinates match the supplied surface, but the moral-topology synthesis is an attributed HFT outlier and remains exploratory.

findings.title: Seed Stewardship Analogy
findings.claim: The doubled waste prohibition can be heard through a seed cycle: scatter is productive when joined to a destination and yield, while the immediate sequel's covering image lets waste appear as provision whose benefit is concealed.
findings.mechanism: The focus Form IV giving carrier meets the registered yield facet only by analogy with the focus's seed-scattering form; the next verse's wasteful actor and covering occurrence complete the attributed sowing-and-stewardship image. This changes waste from a loss of stock alone into dispersal without cared-for consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see a material image of accountable consequence: the contrast is between directed provision and scatter without a productive destination.
findings.containment: The focus imperative remains give, not grow. The crop and seed-cover stages are an exploratory analogy grounded in root and context nominations; the passage does not describe literal cultivation.

epistemic.reason: All HFT roots and coordinates match supplied occurrences, but the agrarian cycle is an attributed, branch-distant outlier; its Form IV carrier restriction is stated explicitly.
